subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-ai.com>, Rebecca Lin <rebecca@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Sanjay / Rebecca,

Great speaking with you both this morning — thanks for walking us through Acme AI's production goals. Quick recap from our side and a set of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity correctly.

Call summary / current asks:
- Preferred deployment mode: Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pool) — you confirmed this is preferred over hosted for predictable latency and data isolation.
- TPS targets: target steady-state ~200 TPS for short requests (<=64 tokens); allow bursts to ~350 TPS for short tails.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent requests estimated at ~120; estimated long-runner concurrent generations ~20 (these are multi-token output sessions).
- Token mix (estimate from your call): ~80% short requests (<=64 tokens total), ~15% medium (65-512 tokens), ~5% long (>512 tokens).
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms for short text-gen; for long multi-turn chat tolerable up to ~1s.
- Models: you indicated using a 70B+ model family for higher-quality responses (we discussed Redwood-2-like variants).
- Data residency: you asked about US-only region and VPC peering for private connectivity (we can support Dedicated + VPC peering).

Initial sizing recommendations (high level):
- GPU suggestion: H100 (recommended) for latency/throughput headroom; A100 80GB is a cost-effective alternative if you accept slightly higher latency.
- Baseline pod: start with 4 x H100s to meet ~200 TPS with continuous batching and our optimized kernels; add autoscaling policy to provide burst capacity to 8 GPUs for peak days.
- Batching / KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated context + batching window tuned to 20-50ms to balance latency and throughput.
- Concurrency config: provision for ~120 concurrent short requests with request queueing and backpressure at 350 TPS cap.

Next steps / asks from you to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm the TPS/concurrency numbers above (200 steady, 350 burst, 120 concurrent).
2) Confirm model family (exact model name or parameter range) — this materially affects memory footprint.
3) Confirm whether Private VPC (customer-managed) is required or if Dedicated with private network + peering is sufficient.

I've attached a sizing workbook (acme-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) with the numbers we discussed and a draft proposal (redwood-proposal-acme.pdf). Rafael, looping you for technical sizing details and ops notes.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize config + draft contract? I can do Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: acme-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, redwood-proposal-acme.pdf, network-diagram.png

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-ai.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming targets: 200 TPS steady, 350 TPS burst, ~120 concurrent is correct.
- GPU preference: we strongly prefer H100s if that gets us under the latency SLO. Cost is secondary for initial launch but we'll want a cost/throughput comparison.
- Models: we plan to run a fine-tuned 70B model (in-house fine-tune of an open model).
- Data residency: must be US-only; VPC peering is required for production (we'll need an ops contact to coordinate).

Can you include a cost estimate (monthly run-rate) for the 4xH100 baseline and for the autoscale to 8xH100? Also, if you can show a comparable A100-based config and delta in expected latency, that would help.

We can do a follow-up Tue morning PT next week (28 Sep is a typo? I mean 1 Sep/2 Sep). 1 Sep 10:00am PT works for Rebecca and me.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure | Acme AI
sanjay@acme-ai.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-ai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi all — quick technical notes based on Marissa's summary and Sanjay's confirmation. I've attached an updated sizing tab in the workbook highlighting throughput numbers.

Technical sizing details:
- Model footprint: a 70B FP16 model with standard KV cache needs ~45-55GB active memory depending on activation tensors and kv-cache per token. This fits on A100/80GB and H100 comfortably; H100 gives better fused-kernel perf.
- Throughput: with Redwood runtime optimizations (prefetch + fused attention) and a batching window of ~30ms, we observe ~50 TPS per H100 for short (<=64 token) requests on this model family. That aligns to ~4 H100 -> 200 TPS baseline.
- Latency: expected P95 for short tokens on 4xH100 with the tuned batching window is ~180-220ms. On equivalent A100 pods the P95 is likely ~250-350ms depending on batch tuning.
- Long requests: medium/long requests should be routed to separate workers or given different batching windows; we recommend reserving 1 GPU of capacity for long-running generations or set concurrency guards so long generations don't starve short requests.
- Autoscaling: configure autoscale to add 2x H100 nodes at 60% CPU/GPU utilization and allow scheduled scaling for business hours. Burst to 8 GPUs expected to handle 350 TPS with modest increase in batching.
- Networking / VPC: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For production we'll need an ops contact to open required CIDR ranges and a short maintenance window for peering validation.

I'll prepare a short ops note with runbook steps (peering, key rotation, monitoring hooks, alerts) and a cost estimate for 4xH100 vs 8xH100 and an A100-based 6xA100 comparison. Expect that to land by EOD tomorrow.

— Rafael
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
